 Parallels and related passages in other Buddhist languages include the Sanskrit *Mahāvastu* (San Lo Mvu 109), the Sanskrit and Tibetan *Udānavarga* (UV 26; Uv Kg 26), Gāndhārī Dharmapada collections (G-Dhp 305–321; G3-Dhp 81–90), and several Chinese translations (T 210.16, T 212.25, T 212.27, T 213.24, and T 213.26).

Text-reuse computations by DharmaNexus reveal that the poem shares numerous formulaic verses with Pali commentarial and sub-commentarial works, including the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, both parts of the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā*, and the *Nettivibhāvinī* [DharmaNexus]. Within the Therāpadāna itself, it shares stock segments with adjacent poems, particularly the *Kaṅkhārevatattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 544), *Rādhattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 541), and *Mogharājattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 542) [DharmaNexus].
